absent: Locking and concurrency rules for subsection bitmap updates outside the online callback mutex.
Full page table teardown sequence and alternate map handling during vmemmap release.
Definition lifetime and reservation layout of alternate maps and device page maps.
Initialization contents and persistence of section usage pageblock flags.
Recovery behavior after failed population beyond immediate error return.
Caller sleep and context constraints for zone relocation and page removal.
Numeric values of section subsection and pageblock size constants.

findings.text: Three helpers provide per level vmemmap table creation for increasing page table depth keyed by address plus node, covering pud then p4d then pgd levels and returning the table pointer for that level.
Range population advances one page at a time from start toward end and stops with an out of memory status on the first address that cannot be populated, otherwise reporting success.

Each level helper checks for an empty entry first, allocates zeroed single page storage on the requested node only in that case, initializes the new table storage, links it into the parent, and returns null when allocation fails.
Mask construction translates the frame interval into an inclusive subsection index interval from the first page to the last page and marks exactly those positions.

Activation builds a temporary mask for the range, rejects an empty mask as invalid, rejects any overlap with already active subsection bits as already existing, otherwise merges the new bits into the section usage record.

Deactivation builds expected and observed masks, warns and aborts with an invalid status when usage is missing or the observed intersection differs from expected, otherwise clears exactly the requested bits.

Section lifecycle combines a subsection occupancy bitmap with separate markers for map presence and present and online and device taint, where filling sets occupancy, clearing removes it, emptiness drives invalidation, and onlining sets the online marker across whole sections.

When the occupancy map becomes empty the section map presence marker is removed and the usage record is released unless it is boot reserved, while descriptor storage is depopulated for ordinary sections and boot storage is freed for early sections, finally clearing the map pointer when empty.
Regular and boot memmap footprint counters are adjusted by signed deltas, with teardown subtracting the estimated descriptor page count for the affected range.
Usage record size accounts for the fixed structure plus trailing flag words whose count derives from section blockflag bit capacity rounded up to whole words.

Index block size is the product of entries per root and per section storage size, using node zeroed slab allocation when slab is ready and early reserved allocation otherwise, with boot failure treated as fatal.

One build reuses an already installed root for repeated subsection adds under hotplug coordination and reports allocation failure, while an alternate build always reports success without installing anything.

Single section setup validates that encoding fits the available map bits, stores the descriptor base minus the section start frame into the map field, preserves unrelated flag bits, then records map presence plus caller flags and the usage pointer.
Present marking advances a global highest present index only when the new index is larger and always sets the present marker on the section.
Zone and node span helpers expose operations to clear contiguity, evaluate contiguity, expand spans on add, shrink spans on remove, recompute node extent, and relocate frame ranges between zones.

Contiguity evaluation walks block aligned windows from zone start to zone end and affirms only if every window resolves to the same zone, with callers clearing beforehand and reevaluating afterward and yielding cooperatively during long scans.

Edge shrinking handles only removal at the current start or end, searching inward at subsection steps for the next online frame matching node and zone and collapsing the zone to empty when no such frame remains.

Node extent is recomputed as the span from the lowest start to the highest end among zones with nonzero span, while range removal poisons descriptors in section bounded pieces and bypasses shrinking for device zones.

Bulk removal first validates alignment and warns on misalignment, then processes section bounded pieces with cooperative scheduling, and per section teardown validates the section before deactivating.

Callback installation and restoration hold an online memory reference and a dedicated mutex, allowing only replacement of the generic handler by one custom handler and restoration back to generic, otherwise reporting invalid.

The generic handler releases pages to the core allocator in hotplug context, while ranged onlining iterates maximal alignment permitted chunks, prepares debug mapping, invokes the current callback per chunk, and finally marks every covered section online.

Descriptor page estimation returns a size proportioned count when optimization is unavailable, a scaled reserve count for small compound orders, and either a single reserve unit on aligned heads or zero on sharing tails for large orders.

Tail sharing is permitted only when the device offset is unaligned and the device map span exceeds one subsection, and tail lookup steps back by one page and resolves the kernel page table entry for that address.

Relocation to a zone clears contiguity, initializes an empty zone, expands zone and node spans, taints edge sections split at subsection granularity for device zones, initializes descriptors, then restores contiguity evaluation.

Descriptor initialization records the highest frame seen, restricts device zones to the driver reserved window, supports deferred early processing, marks hotplugged frames as offline or reserved, and sets block migratetype at aligned boundaries with cooperative scheduling.
Several paths dereference section usage or assume zone coverage without showing additional guards, so callers must ensure prior activation and span inclusion to avoid invalid access.
A weak empty hook permits platform specific reporting after vmemmap population without affecting default behavior.
Negative status codes signal allocation or population failure and invalid empty or mismatched subsection operations and duplicate activation, with zero indicating success.
